'''David Fowler''' (born 1 June 1950)<ref>{{cite web |title=Fowler, Prof. David |url=https://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540884.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-43460 |website=Who's Who science|environmental physicist]], recognized as an authority on [[air pollution|atmospheric pollution]].<ref>{{cite web |title=World authority on air pollution retires after 42-year career at Centre |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2021/11/03/net-zero-policies-could-create-new-pollution-risks-warns-royal/ |access-date=11 February 2022 |work=The Telegraph |date=3 November 2021 == Education and career ==

Fowler gained a B.Sc. in [[environmental physics]] at the [[University of Nottingham]] in 1972, followed by a Ph.D. at the same university in 1976, before moving to the Institute of Terrestrial Ecology in [[Edinburgh]] (later incorporated into the [[Centre for Ecology & Hydrology]]), where he spent the next four decades of his career. He has authored around 250 peer-reviewed papers.<ref name="fowler1">{{cite web |title=Professor David Fowler: Professional Summary |url=https://www.ceh.ac.uk/staff/david-fowler |publisher=UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology |access-date=11 February 2022}}</ref><ref name="googlescholar">{{cite web |title=David Fowler |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=OUZkrDQAAAAJ|access-date=5 January 2025}}</ref>

== Policy work ==

Apart from scientific research, Fowler has also worked on the application of air quality science to public policy in both the UK and Europe.<ref name="fowler1"/> He has been a member of around two dozen scientific committees, including the [[Royal Society]] Global Environmental Research Committee (of which he has been chair since 2011), and the [[Air Quality Expert Group]], of which he is an ad-hoc member.<ref>{{cite web |title=About the Air Quality Expert Group |url=https://uk-air.defra.gov.uk/research/aqeg/about |website=gov.uk |publisher=Department for Environment Food & Rural Affairs |access-date=11 January 2022 |archive-date=23 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211223145516/https://uk-air.defra.gov.uk/research/aqeg/about |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2008, Fowler chaired a committee of European air pollution experts to produce a major study of [[ground-level ozone]] for the Royal Society, which concluded "that existing emission controls will not be sufficient to reduce ozone concentrations to levels acceptable for human health and environmental protection" and called "for renewed global action to address ozone and its precursors".<ref>{{cite web|title=Ground-level ozone in the 21st century: future trends, impacts and policy implications|website=The Royal Society|access-date=3 June 2023|url=https://royalsociety.org/topics-policy/publications/2008/ground-level-ozone/|date=6 October 2008|archive-date=4 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230604014645/https://royalsociety.org/topics-policy/publications/2008/ground-level-ozone/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Awards ==

Fowler became an honorary professor of the University of Nottingham in 1991, was elected a [[Fellowship of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 1999, and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] of London in 2002. He was awarded the [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]] in 2005 for services to atmospheric sciences.<ref name="fowler1"/>
